-- IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY,
-- FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE
-- AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER
-- LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM,
-- OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE
-- SOFTWARE.

--!optimize 2
local Types = require(script.Types)

--[=[
    @class Iris

    Iris; contains the all user-facing functions and properties.
    A set of internal functions can be found in `Iris.Internal` (only use if you understand).

    In its simplest form, users may start Iris by using
    ```lua
    Iris.Init()

    Iris:Connect(function()
        Iris.Window({"My First Window!"})
            Iris.Text({"Hello, World"})
            Iris.Button({"Save"})
            Iris.InputNum({"Input"})
        Iris.End()
    end)
    ```
]=]
local Iris = {} :: Types.Iris

local Internal: Types.Internal = require(script.Internal)(Iris)

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @prop Disabled boolean

    While Iris.Disabled is true, execution of Iris and connected functions will be paused.
    The widgets are not destroyed, they are just frozen so no changes will happen to them.
]=]
Iris.Disabled = false

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @prop Args { [string]: { [string]: any } }

    Provides a list of every possible Argument for each type of widget to it's index.
    For instance, `Iris.Args.Window.NoResize`.
    The Args table is useful for using widget Arguments without remembering their order.
    ```lua
    Iris.Window({"My Window", [Iris.Args.Window.NoResize] = true})
    ```
]=]
Iris.Args = {}

--[=[
    @ignore
    @within Iris
    @prop Events table

    -todo: work out what this is used for.
]=]
Iris.Events = {}

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function Init
    @param parentInstance Instance? -- where Iris will place widgets UIs under, defaulting to [PlayerGui]
    @param eventConnection (RBXScriptSignal | () -> () | false)? -- the event to determine an Iris cycle, defaulting to [Heartbeat]
    @param allowMultipleInits boolean? -- allows subsequent calls 'Iris.Init()' to do nothing rather than error about initialising again, defaulting to false
    @return Iris

    Initializes Iris and begins rendering. Can only be called once.
    See [Iris.Shutdown] to stop Iris, or [Iris.Disabled] to temporarily disable Iris.

    Once initialized, [Iris:Connect] can be used to create a widget.

    If the `eventConnection` is `false` then Iris will not create a cycle loop and the user will need to call [Internal._cycle] every frame.
]=]
function Iris.Init(parentInstance: BasePlayerGui | GuiBase2d?, eventConnection: (RBXScriptSignal | (() -> number) | false)?, allowMultipleInits: boolean?): Types.Iris
    assert(Internal._shutdown == false, "Iris.Init() cannot be called once shutdown.")
    assert(Internal._started == false or allowMultipleInits == true, "Iris.Init() can only be called once.")

    if Internal._started then
        return Iris
    end

    if parentInstance == nil then
        -- coalesce to playerGui
        parentInstance = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
    end
    if eventConnection == nil then
        -- coalesce to Heartbeat
        eventConnection = game:GetService("RunService").Heartbeat
    end
    Internal.parentInstance = parentInstance :: BasePlayerGui | GuiBase2d
    Internal._started = true

    Internal._generateRootInstance()
    Internal._generateSelectionImageObject()

    for _, callback in Internal._initFunctions do
        callback()
    end

    -- spawns the connection to call `Internal._cycle()` within.
    task.spawn(function()
        if typeof(eventConnection) == "function" then
            while Internal._started do
                local deltaTime = eventConnection()
                Internal._cycle(deltaTime)
            end
        elseif eventConnection ~= nil and eventConnection ~= false then
            Internal._eventConnection = eventConnection:Connect(function(...)
                Internal._cycle(...)
            end)
        end
    end)

    return Iris
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function Shutdown

    Shuts Iris down. This can only be called once, and Iris cannot be started once shut down.
]=]
function Iris.Shutdown()
    Internal._started = false
    Internal._shutdown = true

    if Internal._eventConnection then
        Internal._eventConnection:Disconnect()
    end
    Internal._eventConnection = nil

    if Internal._rootWidget then
        if Internal._rootWidget.Instance then
            Internal._widgets["Root"].Discard(Internal._rootWidget)
        end
        Internal._rootInstance = nil
    end

    if Internal.SelectionImageObject then
        Internal.SelectionImageObject:Destroy()
    end

    for _, connection in Internal._connections do
        connection:Disconnect()
    end
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @method Connect
    @param callback () -> () -- the callback containg the Iris code
    @return () -> () -- call to disconnect it

    Connects a function which will execute every Iris cycle. [Iris.Init] must be called before connecting.

    A cycle is determined by the `eventConnection` passed to [Iris.Init] (default to [RunService.Heartbeat]).

    Multiple callbacks can be added to Iris from many different scripts or modules.
]=]
function Iris:Connect(callback: () -> ()): () -> () -- this uses method syntax for no reason.
    if Internal._started == false then
        warn("Iris:Connect() was called before calling Iris.Init(); always initialise Iris first.")
    end
    local connectionIndex = #Internal._connectedFunctions + 1
    Internal._connectedFunctions[connectionIndex] = callback
    return function()
        Internal._connectedFunctions[connectionIndex] = nil
    end
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function Append
    @param userInstance GuiObject -- the Roblox [Instance] to insert into Iris

    Inserts any Roblox [Instance] into Iris.

    The parent of the inserted instance can either be determined by the `_config.Parent`
    property or by the current parent widget from the stack.
]=]
function Iris.Append(userInstance: GuiObject)
    local parentWidget = Internal._GetParentWidget()
    local widgetInstanceParent: GuiObject
    if Internal._config.Parent then
        widgetInstanceParent = Internal._config.Parent :: any
    else
        widgetInstanceParent = Internal._widgets[parentWidget.type].ChildAdded(parentWidget, { type = "userInstance" } :: Types.Widget)
    end
    userInstance.Parent = widgetInstanceParent
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function End

    Marks the end of any widgets which contain children. For example:
    ```lua
    -- Widgets placed here **will not** be inside the tree
    Iris.Text({"Above and outside the tree"})

    -- A Tree widget can contain children.
    -- We must therefore remember to call `Iris.End()`
    Iris.Tree({"My First Tree"})
        -- Widgets placed here **will** be inside the tree
        Iris.Text({"Tree item 1"})
        Iris.Text({"Tree item 2"})
    Iris.End()

    -- Widgets placed here **will not** be inside the tree
    Iris.Text({"Below and outside the tree"})
    ```
    :::caution Caution: Error
    Seeing the error `Callback has too few calls to Iris.End()` or `Callback has too many calls to Iris.End()`?
    Using the wrong amount of `Iris.End()` calls in your code will lead to an error.

    Each widget called which might have children should be paired with a call to `Iris.End()`, **even if the Widget doesnt currently have any children**.
    :::
]=]
function Iris.End()
    if Internal._stackIndex == 1 then
        error("Too many calls to Iris.End().", 2)
    end

    Internal._IDStack[Internal._stackIndex] = nil
    Internal._stackIndex -= 1
end

--[[
    ------------------------
        [SECTION] Config
    ------------------------
]]

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function ForceRefresh

    Destroys and regenerates all instances used by Iris. Useful if you want to propogate state changes.
    :::caution Caution: Performance
    Because this function Deletes and Initializes many instances, it may cause **performance issues** when used with many widgets.
    In **no** case should it be called every frame.
    :::
]=]
function Iris.ForceRefresh()
    Internal._globalRefreshRequested = true
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function UpdateGlobalConfig
    @param deltaStyle { [string]: any } -- a table containing the changes in style ex: `{ItemWidth = UDim.new(0, 100)}`

    Customizes the configuration which **every** widget will inherit from.

    It can be used along with [Iris.TemplateConfig] to easily swap styles, for example:
    ```lua
    Iris.UpdateGlobalConfig(Iris.TemplateConfig.colorLight) -- use light theme
    ```
    :::caution Caution: Performance
    This function internally calls [Iris.ForceRefresh] so that style changes are propogated.

    As such, it may cause **performance issues** when used with many widgets.
    In **no** case should it be called every frame.
    :::
]=]
function Iris.UpdateGlobalConfig(deltaStyle: { [string]: any })
    for index, style in deltaStyle do
        Internal._rootConfig[index] = style
    end
    Iris.ForceRefresh()
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function PushConfig
    @param deltaStyle { [string]: any } -- a table containing the changes in style ex: `{ItemWidth = UDim.new(0, 100)}`

    Allows cascading of a style by allowing styles to be locally and hierarchically applied.

    Each call to Iris.PushConfig must be paired with a call to [Iris.PopConfig], for example:
    ```lua
    Iris.Text({"boring text"})

    Iris.PushConfig({TextColor = Color3.fromRGB(128, 0, 256)})
        Iris.Text({"Colored Text!"})
    Iris.PopConfig()

    Iris.Text({"boring text"})
    ```
]=]
function Iris.PushConfig(deltaStyle: { [string]: any })
    local ID = Iris.State(-1)
    if ID.value == -1 then
        ID:set(deltaStyle)
    else
        -- compare tables
        if Internal._deepCompare(ID:get(), deltaStyle) == false then
            -- refresh local
            ID:set(deltaStyle)
            Internal._refreshStack[Internal._refreshLevel] = true
            Internal._refreshCounter += 1
        end
    end
    Internal._refreshLevel += 1

    Internal._config = setmetatable(deltaStyle, {
        __index = Internal._config,
    }) :: any
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function PopConfig

    Ends a [Iris.PushConfig] style.

    Each call to [Iris.PopConfig] should match a call to [Iris.PushConfig].
]=]
function Iris.PopConfig()
    Internal._refreshLevel -= 1
    if Internal._refreshStack[Internal._refreshLevel] == true then
        Internal._refreshCounter -= 1
        Internal._refreshStack[Internal._refreshLevel] = nil
    end

    Internal._config = getmetatable(Internal._config :: any).__index
end

--[=[

    @within Iris
    @prop TemplateConfig { [string]: { [string]: any } }

    TemplateConfig provides a table of default styles and configurations which you may apply to your UI.
]=]
Iris.TemplateConfig = require(script.config)
Iris.UpdateGlobalConfig(Iris.TemplateConfig.colorDark) -- use colorDark and sizeDefault themes by default
Iris.UpdateGlobalConfig(Iris.TemplateConfig.sizeDefault)
Iris.UpdateGlobalConfig(Iris.TemplateConfig.utilityDefault)
Internal._globalRefreshRequested = false -- UpdatingGlobalConfig changes this to true, leads to Root being generated twice.

--[[
    --------------------
        [SECTION] ID
    --------------------
]]

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function PushId
    @param id ID -- custom id

    Pushes an id onto the id stack for all future widgets. Use [Iris.PopId] to pop it off the stack.
]=]
function Iris.PushId(ID: Types.ID)
    assert(typeof(ID) == "string", "The ID argument to Iris.PushId() to be a string.")

    Internal._newID = true
    table.insert(Internal._pushedIds, ID)
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function PopID

    Removes the most recent pushed id from the id stack.
]=]
function Iris.PopId()
    if #Internal._pushedIds == 0 then
        return
    end

    table.remove(Internal._pushedIds)
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function SetNextWidgetID
    @param id ID -- custom id.

    Sets the id for the next widget. Useful for using [Iris.Append] on the same widget.
    ```lua
    Iris.SetNextWidgetId("demo_window")
    Iris.Window({ "Window" })
        Iris.Text({ "Text one placed here." })
    Iris.End()

    -- later in the code

    Iris.SetNextWidgetId("demo_window")
    Iris.Window()
        Iris.Text({ "Text two placed here." })
    Iris.End()

    -- both text widgets will be placed under the same window despite being called separately.
    ```
]=]
function Iris.SetNextWidgetID(ID: Types.ID)
    Internal._nextWidgetId = ID
end

--[[
    -----------------------
        [SECTION] State
    -----------------------
]]

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function State<T>
    @param initialValue T -- the initial value for the state
    @return State<T>
    @tag State

    Constructs a new [State] object. Subsequent ID calls will return the same object.
    :::info
    Iris.State allows you to create "references" to the same value while inside your UI drawing loop.
    For example:
    ```lua
    Iris:Connect(function()
        local myNumber = 5
        myNumber = myNumber + 1
        Iris.Text({"The number is: " .. myNumber})
    end)
    ```
    This is problematic. Each time the function is called, a new myNumber is initialized, instead of retrieving the old one.
    The above code will always display 6.
    ***
    Iris.State solves this problem:
    ```lua
    Iris:Connect(function()
        local myNumber = Iris.State(5)
        myNumber:set(myNumber:get() + 1)
        Iris.Text({"The number is: " .. myNumber})
    end)
    ```
    In this example, the code will work properly, and increment every frame.
    :::
]=]
function Iris.State<T>(initialValue: T)
    local ID = Internal._getID(2)
    if Internal._states[ID] then
        return Internal._states[ID]
    end
    local newState = {
        ID = ID,
        value = initialValue,
        lastChangeTick = Iris.Internal._cycleTick,
        ConnectedWidgets = {},
        ConnectedFunctions = {},
    } :: Types.State<T>
    setmetatable(newState, Internal.StateClass)
    Internal._states[ID] = newState
    return newState
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function WeakState<T>
    @param initialValue T -- the initial value for the state
    @return State<T>
    @tag State

    Constructs a new state object, subsequent ID calls will return the same object, except all widgets connected to the state are discarded, the state reverts to the passed initialValue
]=]
function Iris.WeakState<T>(initialValue: T)
    local ID = Internal._getID(2)
    if Internal._states[ID] then
        if next(Internal._states[ID].ConnectedWidgets) == nil then
            Internal._states[ID] = nil
        else
            return Internal._states[ID]
        end
    end
    local newState = {
        ID = ID,
        value = initialValue,
        lastChangeTick = Iris.Internal._cycleTick,
        ConnectedWidgets = {},
        ConnectedFunctions = {},
    } :: Types.State<T>
    setmetatable(newState, Internal.StateClass)
    Internal._states[ID] = newState
    return newState
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function VariableState<T>
    @param variable T -- the variable to track
    @param callback (T) -> () -- a function which sets the new variable locally
    @return State<T>
    @tag State

    Returns a state object linked to a local variable.

    The passed variable is used to check whether the state object should update. The callback method is used to change the local variable when the state changes.

    The existence of such a function is to make working with local variables easier.
    Since Iris cannot directly manipulate the memory of the variable, like in C++, it must instead rely on the user updating it through the callback provided.
    Additionally, because the state value is not updated when created or called we cannot return the new value back, instead we require a callback for the user to update.

    ```lua
    local myNumber = 5

    local state = Iris.VariableState(myNumber, function(value)
        myNumber = value
    end)
    Iris.DragNum({ "My number" }, { number = state })
    ```

    This is how Dear ImGui does the same in C++ where we can just provide the memory location to the variable which is then updated directly.
    ```cpp
    static int myNumber = 5;
    ImGui::DragInt("My number", &myNumber); // Here in C++, we can directly pass the variable.
    ```

    :::caution Caution: Update Order
    If the variable and state value are different when calling this, the variable value takes precedence.

    Therefore, if you update the state using `state.value = ...` then it will be overwritten by the variable value.
    You must use `state:set(...)` if you want the variable to update to the state's value.
    :::
]=]
function Iris.VariableState<T>(variable: T, callback: (T) -> ())
    local ID = Internal._getID(2)
    local state = Internal._states[ID]

    if state then
        if variable ~= state.value then
            state:set(variable)
        end
        return state
    end

    local newState = {
        ID = ID,
        value = variable,
        lastChangeTick = Iris.Internal._cycleTick,
        ConnectedWidgets = {},
        ConnectedFunctions = {},
    } :: Types.State<T>
    setmetatable(newState, Internal.StateClass)
    Internal._states[ID] = newState

    newState:onChange(callback)

    return newState
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function TableState<K, V>
    @param table { [K]: V } -- the table containing the value
    @param key K -- the key to the value in table
    @param callback ((newValue: V) -> false?)? -- a function called when the state is changed
    @return State<V>
    @tag State

    Similar to Iris.VariableState but takes a table and key to modify a specific value and a callback to determine whether to update the value.

    The passed table and key are used to check the value. The callback is called when the state changes value and determines whether we update the table.
    This is useful if we want to monitor a table value which needs to call other functions when changed.

    Since tables are pass-by-reference, we can modify the table anywhere and it will update all other instances. Therefore, we don't need a callback by default.
    ```lua
    local data = {
        myNumber = 5
    }

    local state = Iris.TableState(data, "myNumber")
    Iris.DragNum({ "My number" }, { number = state })
    ```

    Here the `data._started` should never be updated directly, only through the `toggle` function. However, we still want to monitor the value and be able to change it.
    Therefore, we use the callback to toggle the function for us and prevent Iris from updating the table value by returning false.
    ```lua
    local data = {
        _started = false
    }

    local function toggle(enabled: boolean)
        data._started = enabled
        if data._started then
            start(...)
        else
            stop(...)
        end
    end

    local state = Iris.TableState(data, "_started", function(stateValue: boolean)
       toggle(stateValue)
       return false
    end)
    Iris.Checkbox({ "Started" }, { isChecked = state })
    ```

    :::caution Caution: Update Order
    If the table value and state value are different when calling this, the table value value takes precedence.

    Therefore, if you update the state using `state.value = ...` then it will be overwritten by the table value.
    You must use `state:set(...)` if you want the table value to update to the state's value.
    :::
]=]
function Iris.TableState<K, V>(tab: { [K]: V }, key: K, callback: ((newValue: V) -> true?)?)
    local value = tab[key]
    local ID = Internal._getID(2)
    local state = Internal._states[ID]

    -- If the table values changes, then we update the state to match.
    if state then
        if value ~= state.value then
            state:set(value)
        end
        return state
    end

    local newState = {
        ID = ID,
        value = value,
        lastChangeTick = Iris.Internal._cycleTick,
        ConnectedWidgets = {},
        ConnectedFunctions = {},
    } :: Types.State<V>
    setmetatable(newState, Internal.StateClass)
    Internal._states[ID] = newState

    -- When a change happens to the state, we update the table value.
    newState:onChange(function()
        if callback ~= nil then
            if callback(newState.value) then
                tab[key] = newState.value
            end
        else
            tab[key] = newState.value
        end
    end)
    return newState
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function ComputedState<T, U>
    @param firstState State<T> -- State to bind to.
    @param onChangeCallback (firstValue: T) -> U -- callback which should return a value transformed from the firstState value
    @return State<U>

    Constructs a new State object, but binds its value to the value of another State.
    :::info
    A common use case for this constructor is when a boolean State needs to be inverted:
    ```lua
    Iris.ComputedState(otherState, function(newValue)
        return not newValue
    end)
    ```
    :::
]=]
function Iris.ComputedState<T, U>(firstState: Types.State<T>, onChangeCallback: (firstValue: T) -> U)
    local ID = Internal._getID(2)

    if Internal._states[ID] then
        return Internal._states[ID]
    else
        local newState = {
            ID = ID,
            value = onChangeCallback(firstState.value),
            lastChangeTick = Iris.Internal._cycleTick,
            ConnectedWidgets = {},
            ConnectedFunctions = {},
        } :: Types.State<T>
        setmetatable(newState, Internal.StateClass)
        Internal._states[ID] = newState

        firstState:onChange(function(newValue: T)
            newState:set(onChangeCallback(newValue))
        end)
        return newState
    end
end

--[=[
    @within Iris
    @function ShowDemoWindow

    ShowDemoWindow is a function which creates a Demonstration window. this window contains many useful utilities for coders,
    and serves as a refrence for using each part of the library. Ideally, the DemoWindow should always be available in your UI.
    It is the same as any other callback you would connect to Iris using [Iris.Connect]
    ```lua
    Iris:Connect(Iris.ShowDemoWindow)
    ```
]=]
Iris.ShowDemoWindow = require(script.demoWindow)(Iris)

require(script.widgets)(Internal)
require(script.API)(Iris)

return Iris

--[[
    Coin Spawner System
    ===================
    A single-place coin spawner: spawns gold coins on the baseplate with a
    hard population cap and a per-coin lifetime, and nothing else.
    
    Location: ServerScriptService
    Execution: Server-side only
    Source: src/CoinSpawner.server.luau — synced by Rojo, do not edit in Studio
--]]

-- ============================================================================
-- CONFIGURATION
-- ============================================================================
-- Easily adjustable parameters - modify these values to customize behavior

local MAX_COINS: number = 50 -- Maximum number of coins allowed simultaneously
local SPAWN_INTERVAL: number = 1 -- Time between spawn cycles (in seconds)
local COIN_LIFETIME: number = 15 -- Duration before each coin auto-despawns (in seconds)
local COIN_SIZE: Vector3 = Vector3.new(0.3, 2, 2) -- Cylinder: X=thickness, Y/Z=diameter
local COIN_COLOR: Color3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 215, 0) -- Gold color (RGB 255, 215, 0)

-- ============================================================================
-- SERVICES
-- ============================================================================

local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

-- ============================================================================
-- COIN FOLDER SETUP
-- ============================================================================
-- Create a dedicated folder to organize all spawned coins
-- This prevents cluttering the Workspace root and improves hierarchy management

local coinFolder: Folder = Instance.new("Folder")
coinFolder.Name = "SpawnedCoins"
coinFolder.Parent = Workspace

-- ============================================================================
-- HELPER FUNCTIONS
-- ============================================================================

--[[
    createCoin
    ----------
    Procedurally generates a coin Part with the specified properties.
    Uses Instance.new() to create the part without referencing ServerStorage.
    
    @param position Vector3 - The world position to spawn the coin
    @return Part - The configured coin instance (not yet parented)
--]]
local function createCoin(position: Vector3): Part
	local coin: Part = Instance.new("Part")

	-- Basic identification
	coin.Name = "Coin"

	-- Visual Properties
	coin.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder -- Cylinder shape for coin appearance
	coin.Color = COIN_COLOR -- Gold/yellow color
	coin.Material = Enum.Material.Neon -- Glowing neon material for high visibility

	-- Physical Properties
	coin.Size = COIN_SIZE
	coin.Anchored = true -- Prevent physics simulation (static position)
	coin.CanCollide = false -- Players can walk through to collect
	coin.Massless = true -- No physics impact on other objects

	-- ========================================================================
	-- POSITIONING USING CFRAME (Modern API)
	-- ========================================================================
	-- Cylinders in Roblox orient their axis along the X-axis by default.
	-- To make the coin stand upright (axis along Y), we rotate 90° around Z.
	--
	-- CFrame composition:
	--   1. CFrame.new(position) - Position at spawn location
	--   2. CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90)) - Rotate to stand upright
	-- ========================================================================

	coin.CFrame = CFrame.new(position) * CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90))

	return coin
end

--[[
    getSpawnBounds
    --------------
    Calculates the spawn area based on the Baseplate's position and size.
    Returns bounds for random coordinate generation.
    
    @return minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ - The X and Z coordinate boundaries
    @return spawnY - The Y coordinate for coins to rest on the baseplate
--]]
local function getSpawnBounds(): (number, number, number, number, number)
	-- Attempt to find the Baseplate in Workspace
	local baseplate: BasePart? = Workspace:FindFirstChild("Baseplate") :: BasePart?

	if not baseplate then
		-- Fallback: Use default values if no baseplate exists
		warn("[CoinSpawner] No Baseplate found in Workspace. Using default spawn bounds.")
		return -50, 50, -50, 50, 1
	end

	-- Extract position and size for coordinate calculations
	local baseplatePosition: Vector3 = baseplate.Position
	local baseplateSize: Vector3 = baseplate.Size

	-- ========================================================================
	-- COORDINATE MATH EXPLANATION
	-- ========================================================================
	-- The spawn area is a rectangle centered on the baseplate.
	--
	-- X BOUNDS CALCULATION:
	--   minX = baseplatePosition.X - (baseplateSize.X / 2)
	--   maxX = baseplatePosition.X + (baseplateSize.X / 2)
	--   This gives us the left and right edges of the baseplate.
	--
	-- Z BOUNDS CALCULATION:
	--   minZ = baseplatePosition.Z - (baseplateSize.Z / 2)
	--   maxZ = baseplatePosition.Z + (baseplateSize.Z / 2)
	--   This gives us the front and back edges of the baseplate.
	--
	-- Y COORDINATE (VERTICAL POSITION):
	--   The coin must rest ON TOP of the baseplate, not inside it.
	--
	--   For a cylinder rotated 90° on Z-axis:
	--   - The original Size.X becomes the vertical height
	--   - Size.Y and Size.Z are the horizontal diameters
	--
	--   Formula:
	--   spawnY = baseplatePosition.Y + (baseplateSize.Y / 2) + (COIN_SIZE.X / 2)
	--
	--   Breaking this down:
	--   - baseplatePosition.Y = center of baseplate
	--   - baseplateSize.Y / 2 = half height (gets us to top surface)
	--   - COIN_SIZE.X / 2 = half coin height (centers coin on surface)
	-- ========================================================================

	local halfSizeX: number = baseplateSize.X / 2
	local halfSizeZ: number = baseplateSize.Z / 2
	local halfCoinHeight: number = COIN_SIZE.X / 2 -- After rotation, X is vertical

	local minX: number = baseplatePosition.X - halfSizeX
	local maxX: number = baseplatePosition.X + halfSizeX
	local minZ: number = baseplatePosition.Z - halfSizeZ
	local maxZ: number = baseplatePosition.Z + halfSizeZ

	-- Calculate Y position: top of baseplate + half coin height
	local spawnY: number = baseplatePosition.Y + (baseplateSize.Y / 2) + halfCoinHeight

	return minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ, spawnY
end

--[[
    spawnCoin
    ---------
    Creates and parents a new coin at a random position within bounds.
    Implements the MAX_COINS limit check and sets up automatic despawn.
--]]
local function spawnCoin(): ()
	-- ========================================================================
	-- LIMIT CHECK
	-- ========================================================================
	-- Count existing coins before spawning a new one
	-- Skip this cycle if the maximum has been reached

	local currentCoinCount: number = #coinFolder:GetChildren()

	if currentCoinCount >= MAX_COINS then
		-- Maximum reached - skip this spawn cycle silently
		return
	end

	-- ========================================================================
	-- RANDOM POSITION GENERATION
	-- ========================================================================
	-- Use Random.new():NextNumber() for smooth floating-point distribution
	-- This provides better randomness quality than math.random()

	local minX: number, maxX: number, minZ: number, maxZ: number, spawnY: number = getSpawnBounds()

	local random: Random = Random.new()
	local randomX: number = random:NextNumber(minX, maxX)
	local randomZ: number = random:NextNumber(minZ, maxZ)

	-- Construct the spawn position vector
	local spawnPosition: Vector3 = Vector3.new(randomX, spawnY, randomZ)

	-- ========================================================================
	-- COIN CREATION AND PARENTING
	-- ========================================================================

	local coin: Part = createCoin(spawnPosition)
	coin.Parent = coinFolder

	-- ========================================================================
	-- LIFECYCLE MANAGEMENT (DESPAWN)
	-- ========================================================================
	-- Use task.delay() for modern, efficient delayed execution
	-- This automatically destroys the coin after COIN_LIFETIME seconds
	--
	-- We check if the coin still exists before destroying to prevent
	-- errors if the coin was manually removed earlier.
	-- ========================================================================

	task.delay(COIN_LIFETIME, function()
		if coin and coin.Parent then
			coin:Destroy()
		end
	end)
end

-- ============================================================================
-- MAIN SPAWN LOOP
-- ============================================================================
-- Continuous spawning at the configured interval
-- Uses task.wait() for modern timing (deprecated wait() is forbidden)

while true do
	spawnCoin()
	task.wait(SPAWN_INTERVAL)
end

-- Extract the CoinSpawner script out of the place file, exactly, and back up the place.
local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")

local PLACE = "Coin Spawner.rbxl"
local OUT = "src/CoinSpawner.server.luau"

-- 1. Back up the place before anything can touch it.
fs.writeDir("backup")
local backup = "backup/Coin Spawner.rbxl"
if not fs.isFile(backup) then
	fs.copy(PLACE, backup)
	print(string.format("backup: %s (%d bytes)", backup, #fs.readFile(backup)))
else
	print(string.format("backup already exists: %s", backup))
end

-- 2. Read the place and pull the script source.
local game = roblox.deserializePlace(fs.readFile(PLACE))
local sss = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local node = sss:FindFirstChild("CoinSpawner")
assert(node, "CoinSpawner not found in ServerScriptService")

local src = (node :: any).Source
assert(type(src) == "string" and #src > 0, "empty source")

-- 3. Write it out untouched.
fs.writeDir("src")
fs.writeFile(OUT, src)

local wrote = fs.readFile(OUT)
print(string.format("wrote: %s", OUT))
print(string.format("chars in place: %d", #src))
print(string.format("chars on disk:  %d", #wrote))
print(string.format("identical: %s", tostring(wrote == src)))
print(string.format("lines: %d", select(2, string.gsub(src, "\n", "\n")) + 1))

-- Rustling: the steal-and-lock half of the ranch. Hold E on a critter behind an OPEN gate to rustle
-- it and carry it home over your head; lock your own gate from inside your ranch (L, the HUD button
-- or the LOCK pad). Rival ranchers' gates open and shut on a clock, and masked rustlers ride in to
-- raid an open ranch, whistling as they come: tag one before it reaches the edge of the map and you
-- get your critter back plus a bounty. Every lock, rustle and tag counts toward the contract board.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Cast = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Cast"))
local Critters = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Critters"))
local Ledger = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Ledger"))
local Pens = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Pens"))
local World = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Workshop"):WaitForChild("World"))

local Rustling = {}

Rustling.CARRY_SCALE = 0.55
Rustling.RAID_EVERY = { 55, 85 }
Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED = 15

local RED = Color3.fromRGB(255, 90, 80)
local GREEN = Color3.fromRGB(130, 255, 120)
local activeRaids: { [Ledger.Account]: boolean } = {}
local rng = Random.new()
local rootOf: (Player) -> BasePart?
local setCarryScale: (Ledger.CritterRecord, number) -> ()

-- Rustle: lift a critter out of an unlocked rival's stall and carry it over your head.
function Rustling.stealFromUnlockedPen(thief: Player, record)
	local thiefAccount = Ledger.accountOf(thief)
	local owner = record.owner
	local root = rootOf(thief)
	if not thiefAccount or not owner or owner == thiefAccount or not root or record.carrier then
		return
	end
	if Ledger.isLocked(owner) then
		Ledger.toast(thiefAccount, owner.name .. "'s gate is LOCKED. Wait for it to open!", RED)
		return
	end
	if thiefAccount.carrying then
		Ledger.toast(thiefAccount, "Your hands are full - run that one home first!", RED)
		return
	end
	if not Pens.freeStallOf(thiefAccount) then
		Ledger.toast(thiefAccount, "No free stall at home for it!", RED)
		return
	end
	Pens.takeCritterFromPen(record)
	record.carrier = thief
	thiefAccount.carrying = record
	local model = record.model
	local prompt = model:FindFirstChild("RustlePrompt", true) :: ProximityPrompt?
	if prompt then
		prompt.Enabled = false
	end
	setCarryScale(record, Rustling.CARRY_SCALE)
	model:SetAttribute("Gait", "carried")
	local critterRoot = model.PrimaryPart :: BasePart
	critterRoot.CFrame = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 3.2, 0)
	critterRoot.Anchored = false
	critterRoot.Massless = true
	local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
	weld.Part0, weld.Part1 = root, critterRoot
	weld.Parent = critterRoot
	model.Parent = workspace
	Ledger.syncRancher(thiefAccount)
	local name = Cast.critterById(record.id).name
	Ledger.toast(thiefAccount, "Rustled " .. name .. "! Run it home to YOUR ranch!", Color3.fromRGB(255, 220, 90))
	Ledger.toast(owner, thief.DisplayName .. " is rustling your " .. name .. "! Lock your gate!", RED)
	Ledger.cue(thiefAccount, "rustle")
	Ledger.cue(owner, "alarm")
end

function rootOf(player: Player): BasePart?
	local character = player.Character
	local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
	if not character or not humanoid or humanoid.Health <= 0 then
		return nil
	end
	return character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart?
end

function setCarryScale(record: Ledger.CritterRecord, scale: number)
	record.model:ScaleTo(scale)
end

-- Locks a rancher's gate for its lock time; a player must be standing inside their own ranch.
function Rustling.lockGate(account: Ledger.Account): boolean
	local plot = account.plot
	if not plot then
		return false
	end
	if account.player then
		local root = rootOf(account.player)
		if not root or not World.ranchContains(plot, root.Position) then
			Ledger.toast(account, "Get inside your ranch to lock the gate!", RED)
			return false
		end
	end
	local now = workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
	if account.lockedUntil > now then
		Ledger.toast(account, string.format("Gate already locked (%ds left)", math.ceil(account.lockedUntil - now)), GREEN)
		return false
	end
	account.lockedUntil = now + Cast.lockSeconds(account.rebirths)
	Ledger.syncRancher(account)
	Ledger.toast(account, "GATE LOCKED for " .. Cast.lockSeconds(account.rebirths) .. "s - your herd is safe", GREEN)
	Ledger.cue(account, "lock")
	Ledger.deed(account, { kind = "lock" })
	return true
end

-- Puts a carried critter back where it came from (or anywhere free in its owner's ranch).
function Rustling.returnCarried(thief: Ledger.Account?, record: Ledger.CritterRecord)
	if thief and thief.carrying == record then
		thief.carrying = nil
		Ledger.syncRancher(thief)
	end
	record.carrier = nil
	local root = record.model.PrimaryPart :: BasePart
	for _, d in root:GetChildren() do
		if d:IsA("WeldConstraint") then
			d:Destroy()
		end
	end
	root.Anchored = true
	setCarryScale(record, 1)
	local owner = record.owner
	if owner and owner.plot and (owner.isBot or (owner.player and owner.player.Parent)) then
		local stall = if record.stall and not owner.stalls[record.stall] then record.stall else Pens.freeStallOf(owner)
		if stall then
			Pens.placeCritterInPen(owner, record, stall, false)
			Critters.poof(root.Position, Color3.fromRGB(230, 200, 140), 12)
			return
		end
	end
	Critters.poof(root.Position, Color3.fromRGB(170, 130, 90), 12)
	record.model:Destroy()
end

-- Every few frames: a carried critter that reaches its thief's ranch moves into a free stall there.
function Rustling.deliverCarriedCritters()
	for _, account in Ledger.players() do
		local record = account.carrying
		if record and account.player then
			local root = rootOf(account.player)
			if not root then
				Rustling.returnCarried(account, record)
			elseif account.plot and World.ranchContains(account.plot, root.Position) then
				local stall = Pens.freeStallOf(account)
				if stall then
					account.carrying = nil
					local critterRoot = record.model.PrimaryPart :: BasePart
					for _, d in critterRoot:GetChildren() do
						if d:IsA("WeldConstraint") then
							d:Destroy()
						end
					end
					setCarryScale(record, 1)
					critterRoot.Anchored = true
					local victim = record.owner
					local name = Cast.critterById(record.id).name
					local rescueRoot = critterRoot.Position
					local prompt = record.model:FindFirstChild("RustlePrompt", true) :: ProximityPrompt?
					if prompt then
						prompt.Enabled = true
					end
					task.spawn(Pens.placeCritterInPen, account, record, stall, true)
					Critters.poof(rescueRoot, Color3.fromRGB(255, 220, 90), 16)
					Ledger.toast(account, "Rustled " .. name .. " home! It earns for YOU now.", GREEN)
					Ledger.cue(account, "delivered")
					if Ledger.discover(account, record.id, record.mutation) then
						Ledger.toast(account, "NEW in your RanchDex: " .. name .. "!", Color3.fromRGB(255, 236, 150))
						Ledger.deed(account, { kind = "discover", id = record.id, mutation = record.mutation })
					end
					Ledger.syncBoard(account)
					Ledger.deed(account, { kind = "rustle", id = record.id, mutation = record.mutation })
					if victim and victim ~= account then
						Ledger.toast(victim, account.name .. " got away with your " .. name .. "!", RED)
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Repaints every gate (bars + countdown) and switches Rustle prompts off behind locked gates.
function Rustling.tickGates()
	local now = workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
	for _, plot in Pens.plots() do
		local owner = Pens.ownerOfPlot(plot.index)
		local locked = owner ~= nil and owner.lockedUntil > now
		World.paintGate(plot, locked, if owner then owner.lockedUntil - now else 0)
		if owner then
			for _, record in owner.stalls do
				local prompt = record.model:FindFirstChild("RustlePrompt", true) :: ProximityPrompt?
				if prompt then
					prompt.Enabled = not locked
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Rival bots lock for a while, then leave the gate open long enough to be rustled from. Each rival
-- (by account order i) gets its own lock and open lengths, so their gates drift out of step.
function Rustling.cycleRivalGates()
	local now = workspace:GetServerTimeNow()
	for i, account in Ledger.allAccounts() do
		if account.isBot and account.lockedUntil < now - 14 - i * 3 then
			account.lockedUntil = now + 18 + i * 4
		end
	end
end

local function rideTo(root: BasePart, target: Vector3, speed: number): Tween
	local from = root.Position
	local goal = Vector3.new(target.X, from.Y, target.Z)
	local heading = if (goal - from).Magnitude > 0.5 then (goal - from).Unit else root.CFrame.LookVector
	local tween = TweenService:Create(root, TweenInfo.new(math.max(0.2, (goal - from).Magnitude / speed), Enum.EasingStyle.Linear), {
		CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(goal, goal + heading),
	})
	tween:Play()
	return tween
end

-- A rustler raid on a player's ranch: warns, rides to the gate, bounces off a locked one, or grabs
-- the best earner and flees for the map edge. Touching the rustler wins the critter back.
function Rustling.sendRustlerRaid(target: Player?)
	local player = target or Players:GetPlayers()[1]
	local account = player and Ledger.accountOf(player)
	if not account or not account.plot or activeRaids[account] then
		return
	end
	local plot = account.plot
	activeRaids[account] = true
	local fromEast = rng:NextNumber() < 0.5
	local edgeX = if fromEast then World.DRIVE_END_X + 20 else World.DRIVE_START_X - 20
	Ledger.toast(account, "A RUSTLER is riding for your ranch! Get home and LOCK your gate (L)!", RED)
	Ledger.cue(account, "whistle")
	player:SetAttribute("RaidEta", workspace:GetServerTimeNow() + 9)

	local model, root = Critters.buildRustler(CFrame.new(edgeX, 0, 0))
	model.Parent = workspace
	local outside = (plot.cf * CFrame.new(0, 0, -World.PLOT_HALF_D - 6)).Position
	local gate = (plot.cf * CFrame.new(0, 0, -World.PLOT_HALF_D + 2)).Position
	local carried: Ledger.CritterRecord? = nil
	local caught = false
	local touch = root.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		local character = player.Character
		if carried and not caught and character and hit:IsDescendantOf(character) then
			caught = true
		end
	end)

	local function finish(text: string, color: Color3)
		touch:Disconnect()
		player:SetAttribute("RaidEta", 0)
		Ledger.toast(account, text, color)
		Critters.poof(root.Position, Color3.fromRGB(170, 130, 90), 20)
		model:Destroy()
		activeRaids[account] = nil
	end

	rideTo(root, outside, Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED).Completed:Wait()
	if Ledger.isLocked(account) or not account.plot then
		root.CFrame *= CFrame.Angles(0, math.pi, 0)
		rideTo(root, Vector3.new(edgeX, 0, 0), Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED * 1.4).Completed:Wait()
		Ledger.cue(account, "lockHeld")
		Ledger.deed(account, { kind = "repel" })
		finish("Your locked gate held! The rustler rode off empty-handed.", GREEN)
		return
	end
	local best: Ledger.CritterRecord? = nil
	for _, record in account.stalls do
		if not best or Cast.incomeOf(record.id, record.mutation, 0) > Cast.incomeOf(best.id, best.mutation, 0) then
			best = record
		end
	end
	if not best then
		rideTo(root, Vector3.new(edgeX, 0, 0), Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED).Completed:Wait()
		finish("The rustler found nothing worth taking.", GREEN)
		return
	end
	local victim = best :: Ledger.CritterRecord
	rideTo(root, gate, Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED).Completed:Wait()
	rideTo(root, (victim.model.PrimaryPart :: BasePart).Position, Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED).Completed:Wait()
	-- The critter left its stall while the rustler rode in (rustled first, or a rebirth cleared the pens).
	if victim.owner ~= account or account.stalls[victim.stall or 0] ~= victim then
		rideTo(root, Vector3.new(edgeX, 0, 0), Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED).Completed:Wait()
		finish("The rustler came up empty-handed and rode off.", GREEN)
		return
	end
	Pens.takeCritterFromPen(victim)
	carried = victim
	victim.carrier = nil
	setCarryScale(victim, Rustling.CARRY_SCALE)
	victim.model:SetAttribute("Gait", "carried")
	local critterRoot = victim.model.PrimaryPart :: BasePart
	critterRoot.CFrame = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 5.5, 0)
	local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
	weld.Part0, weld.Part1 = root, critterRoot
	weld.Parent = critterRoot
	critterRoot.Anchored = false
	victim.model.Parent = workspace
	local name = Cast.critterById(victim.id).name
	Ledger.toast(account, "The rustler grabbed your " .. name .. "! Tag them before they reach the edge!", RED)
	Ledger.cue(account, "alarm")
	for _, waypoint in { gate, outside, Vector3.new(edgeX + (if fromEast then 40 else -40), 0, 0) } do
		local ride = rideTo(root, waypoint, Rustling.RUSTLER_SPEED * 0.8)
		while ride.PlaybackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Playing and not caught do
			local chaser = rootOf(player)
			if chaser and (chaser.Position - root.Position).Magnitude < 5.5 then
				caught = true
			end
			task.wait(0.05)
		end
		if caught then
			ride:Cancel()
			break
		end
	end
	if caught then
		Rustling.returnCarried(nil, victim)
		-- the bounty: eight seconds of your herd's income, at least $80, at most a quarter of your cash
		local bounty = math.max(80, math.min(math.floor(Ledger.incomeOf(account) * 8), math.floor(account.cash * 0.25)))
		Ledger.addCash(account, bounty)
		Ledger.cue(account, "tag", bounty)
		Ledger.deed(account, { kind = "tag", amount = bounty })
		finish("You tackled the rustler! " .. name .. " is home, plus a " .. Cast.formatCash(bounty) .. " bounty.", GREEN)
	else
		victim.model:Destroy()
		Ledger.cue(account, "fail")
		finish("The rustler got away with your " .. name .. "...", RED)
	end
end

function Rustling.startRustlingWatch()
	Pens.rustleHandler = Rustling.stealFromUnlockedPen
	for _, plot in Pens.plots() do
		plot.lockPad.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
			local player = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
			local owner = Pens.ownerOfPlot(plot.index)
			if player and owner and owner.player == player and not Ledger.isLocked(owner) then
				Rustling.lockGate(owner)
			end
		end)
	end
	local acc = 0
	RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
		acc += dt
		if acc >= 0.2 then
			acc = 0
			Rustling.deliverCarriedCritters()
			Rustling.tickGates()
			Rustling.cycleRivalGates()
		end
	end)
	task.spawn(function()
		while true do
			task.wait(rng:NextInteger(Rustling.RAID_EVERY[1], Rustling.RAID_EVERY[2]))
			for _, account in Ledger.players() do
				local herd = 0
				for _ in account.stalls do
					herd += 1
				end
				if herd >= 2 and account.player then
					task.spawn(Rustling.sendRustlerRaid, account.player)
				end
			end
		end
	end)
end

return Rustling

        hasState = true,
        hasChildren = false,
        Args = {
            ["Text"] = 1,
        },
        Events = {
            ["checked"] = {
                ["Init"] = function(_thisWidget: Types.Checkbox) end,
                ["Get"] = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
                    return thisWidget.lastCheckedTick == Iris._cycleTick
                end,
            },
            ["unchecked"] = {
                ["Init"] = function(_thisWidget: Types.Checkbox) end,
                ["Get"] = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
                    return thisWidget.lastUncheckedTick == Iris._cycleTick
                end,
            },
            ["hovered"] = widgets.EVENTS.hover(function(thisWidget: Types.Widget)
                return thisWidget.Instance
            end),
        },
        Generate = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
            local Checkbox = Instance.new("TextButton")
            Checkbox.Name = "Iris_Checkbox"
            Checkbox.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY
            Checkbox.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0)
            Checkbox.BackgroundTransparency = 1
            Checkbox.BorderSizePixel = 0
            Checkbox.Text = ""
            Checkbox.AutoButtonColor = false
            
            widgets.UIListLayout(Checkbox, Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal, UDim.new(0, Iris._config.ItemInnerSpacing.X)).VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Center

            local checkboxSize = Iris._config.TextSize + 2 * Iris._config.FramePadding.Y

            local Box = Instance.new("Frame")
            Box.Name = "Box"
            Box.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(checkboxSize, checkboxSize)
            Box.BackgroundColor3 = Iris._config.FrameBgColor
            Box.BackgroundTransparency = Iris._config.FrameBgTransparency
            
            widgets.applyFrameStyle(Box, true)
            widgets.UIPadding(Box, Vector2.new(math.floor(checkboxSize / 10), math.floor(checkboxSize / 10)))

            widgets.applyInteractionHighlights("Background", Checkbox, Box, {
                Color = Iris._config.FrameBgColor,
                Transparency = Iris._config.FrameBgTransparency,
                HoveredColor = Iris._config.FrameBgHoveredColor,
                HoveredTransparency = Iris._config.FrameBgHoveredTransparency,
                ActiveColor = Iris._config.FrameBgActiveColor,
                ActiveTransparency = Iris._config.FrameBgActiveTransparency,
            })

            Box.Parent = Checkbox

            local Checkmark = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
            Checkmark.Name = "Checkmark"
            Checkmark.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
            Checkmark.BackgroundTransparency = 1
            Checkmark.Image = widgets.ICONS.CHECKMARK
            Checkmark.ImageColor3 = Iris._config.CheckMarkColor
            Checkmark.ImageTransparency = 1
            Checkmark.ScaleType = Enum.ScaleType.Fit

            Checkmark.Parent = Box

            widgets.applyButtonClick(Checkbox, function()
                thisWidget.state.isChecked:set(not thisWidget.state.isChecked.value)
            end)

            local TextLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel")
            TextLabel.Name = "TextLabel"
            TextLabel.AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.XY
            TextLabel.BackgroundTransparency = 1
            TextLabel.BorderSizePixel = 0
            TextLabel.LayoutOrder = 1

            widgets.applyTextStyle(TextLabel)
            TextLabel.Parent = Checkbox

            return Checkbox
        end,
        GenerateState = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
            if thisWidget.state.isChecked == nil then
                thisWidget.state.isChecked = Iris._widgetState(thisWidget, "checked", false)
            end
        end,
        Update = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
            local Checkbox = thisWidget.Instance :: TextButton
            Checkbox.TextLabel.Text = thisWidget.arguments.Text or "Checkbox"
        end,
        UpdateState = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
            local Checkbox = thisWidget.Instance :: TextButton
            local Box = Checkbox.Box :: Frame
            local Checkmark: ImageLabel = Box.Checkmark
            if thisWidget.state.isChecked.value then
                Checkmark.ImageTransparency = Iris._config.CheckMarkTransparency
                thisWidget.lastCheckedTick = Iris._cycleTick + 1
            else
                Checkmark.ImageTransparency = 1
                thisWidget.lastUncheckedTick = Iris._cycleTick + 1
            end
        end,
        Discard = function(thisWidget: Types.Checkbox)
            thisWidget.Instance:Destroy()
            widgets.discardState(thisWidget)
        end,
    } :: Types.WidgetClass)
end

-- Probe: read the place with Lune and report every script's path, class and source.
-- Read-only. Writes nothing.
local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")

local PLACE = "Coin Spawner.rbxl"

local data = fs.readFile(PLACE)
print(string.format("read %s (%d bytes)", PLACE, #data))

local game = roblox.deserializePlace(data)
print("deserialized ok")

local function pathOf(inst: Instance): string
	local parts = {}
	local cur: Instance? = inst
	while cur and cur ~= game do
		table.insert(parts, 1, cur.Name)
		cur = cur.Parent
	end
	return table.concat(parts, ".")
end

print("\n== top-level children ==")
for _, child in game:GetChildren() do
	print(string.format("  %-22s [%-22s] children=%d", child.Name, child.ClassName, #child:GetChildren()))
end

print("\n== source containers ==")
local count = 0
for _, d in game:GetDescendants() do
	local cn = d.ClassName
	if cn == "Script" or cn == "LocalScript" or cn == "ModuleScript" then
		count += 1
		local src = (d :: any).Source
		print(string.format(
			"  %s [%s] parent=%s chars=%s",
			pathOf(d),
			cn,
			d.Parent and d.Parent.Name or "nil",
			src and tostring(#src) or "nil"
		))
		if src and #src > 0 then
			print("  --- first 160 ---")
			print(src:sub(1, 160))
			print("  --- last 100 ---")
			print(src:sub(-100))
		end
	end
end
print(string.format("\ncontainers: %d", count))

-- Showcase: shortcuts to each screen of Rot Ranch for a Studio play-test, a reviewer or TOUR.json.
-- Showcase.stage("cover" | "lasso" | "herd" | "stampede" | "goldenhour" | "dustdevil" | "raid") sets
-- the first player's ranch up for that beat; ServerStorage.RanchShowcase (a BindableFunction)
-- takes the finer commands: cash, rebirths, herd, lock, guide, dex, and any event by name.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")

local Cast = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Cast"))
local CattleDrive = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("CattleDrive"))
local Events = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Events"))
local Guide = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Guide"))
local Ledger = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Ledger"))
local Pens = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Pens"))
local Rustling = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Rustling"))
local World = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild("Workshop"):WaitForChild("World"))

local Showcase = {}

-- A herd that shows every mutation and the top of the ladder.
Showcase.HERD = {
	{ "udderlord" }, { "haybalehydra", "Golden" }, { "moothership" }, { "jackalope", "Spicy" }, { "wienerbago", "Crystal" },
	{ "brisketbronco" }, { "banjobuzzard", "Ghost" }, { "hamwich", "Golden" }, { "cactopus", "Moldy" }, { "skelecow" },
}

local function firstAccount(): (Player?, Ledger.Account?)
	local player = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
	return player, player and Ledger.accountOf(player)
end

local function clearHerd(account: Ledger.Account)
	for stall, record in account.stalls do
		record.model:Destroy()
		account.stalls[stall] = nil
	end
end

-- Lassoes a critter right next to the first player, with a slow flight so the rope hangs in the air.
local function showLasso(player: Player, account: Ledger.Account)
	local character = player.Character
	local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart?
	if not root or not account.plot then
		return
	end
	local x = account.plot.cf.Position.X - 8
	local side = if account.plot.cf.Position.Z < 0 then -1 else 1
	character:PivotTo(CFrame.lookAt(Vector3.new(x, 3.2, side * 13), Vector3.new(x + 6, 3.2, 0)))
	task.wait(0.3)
	local entry = CattleDrive.spawnDriveCritter("toastallion", "Golden")
	local span = World.DRIVE_END_X - World.DRIVE_START_X
	CattleDrive.fastForward(entry, math.clamp((x + 7 - World.DRIVE_START_X) / span, 0, 1))
	account.cash = math.max(account.cash, entry.price + 500)
	Ledger.syncRancher(account)
	task.wait(0.2)
	CattleDrive.lassoFlight = 3.2
	task.spawn(CattleDrive.lassoCritter, player, entry)
	task.delay(4, function()
		CattleDrive.lassoFlight = 1
	end)
end

-- Runs one finer command; returns true when it did something.
function Showcase.run(command: string, arg: any?): boolean
	local player, account = firstAccount()
	if command == "stampede" or command == "goldenhour" or command == "dustdevil" then
		task.spawn(Events.trigger, command)
	elseif command == "raid" and player then
		task.spawn(Rustling.sendRustlerRaid, player)
	elseif not (player and account) then
		return false
	elseif command == "rebirths" then
		account.rebirths = tonumber(arg) or 0
		Pens.paintRanch(account)
		Ledger.syncRancher(account)
	elseif command == "cash" then
		Ledger.addCash(account, tonumber(arg) or 1000)
	elseif command == "herd" then
		clearHerd(account)
		for i = 1, math.min(tonumber(arg) or #Showcase.HERD, #Showcase.HERD, Cast.stallsFor(account.rebirths)) do
			Pens.stockCritter(account, Showcase.HERD[i][1], Showcase.HERD[i][2])
		end
	elseif command == "lock" then
		account.lockedUntil = workspace:GetServerTimeNow() + (tonumber(arg) or 40)
		Ledger.syncRancher(account)
	elseif command == "guide" then
		Guide.skipTo(account, tonumber(arg) or Guide.DONE)
	elseif command == "dex" then
		-- Everything but the last few rungs, so the book shows both found and ??? cards.
		for i, critter in Cast.CRITTERS do
			if i <= (tonumber(arg) or 17) then
				Ledger.discover(account, critter.id, nil)
			end
		end
		Ledger.syncBoard(account)
	elseif command == "lasso" then
		task.spawn(showLasso, player, account)
	else
		return false
	end
	return true
end

-- One screen per call, for TOUR.json: "cover", "lasso", "herd", "raid" or an event name.
function Showcase.stage(name: string)
	local _, account = firstAccount()
	if account and (name == "cover" or name == "herd") then
		Showcase.run("rebirths", 2)
		Showcase.run("herd")
		Showcase.run("cash", 45000 - account.cash)
		Showcase.run("dex")
		Showcase.run("guide", Guide.DONE)
	end
	if name == "cover" then
		Showcase.run("goldenhour")
	elseif name == "lasso" or name == "stampede" or name == "goldenhour" or name == "dustdevil" or name == "raid" then
		Showcase.run(name)
	end
end

function Showcase.bind()
	local showcase = Instance.new("BindableFunction")
	showcase.Name = "RanchShowcase"
	showcase.OnInvoke = Showcase.run
	showcase.Parent = ServerStorage
end

return Showcase
